belief: What the media says is normal must be right.
origins: Television, streaming, music, news, and social media shape what feels ordinary: how people speak, treat each other, spend, relate, and think. Because we see it so often, it can seem like everyone does it and so it must be fine. Over time, we may adopt values without noticing.
teaches: Paul writes, “Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.” Isaiah warns, “Woe to those who call evil good and good evil.” Proverbs says, “There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.” Philippians 4:8 gives a filter: “whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable.” Common is not the same as right.
self_statements: Everyone does it, so it is fine.
If it is on TV, it is normal.
I do not need to question what I watch.
That is just how people live now.
If it is everywhere, it must be acceptable.
errors: Treating media as a moral authority.
Feeling comfortable and concluding that it is good.
questions: What values does the media I consume promote?
How have those messages shaped what I expect from relationships, money, or myself?
What does Scripture say is true, honorable, and lovely?
What would I think of this if I had never seen it on screen?
How does my media diet affect my mood and faith?
What would I change in what I watch or listen to?
truth: Popular is not the same as right. I can test what I see and hear against God’s word, choose what I take in, and let my mind be renewed.
hw_truths: I can test everything against God’s word.
A way that seems right can lead astray.
I can think on what is true and lovely.
I choose what I take in.
log: Each week, note one message you tested against Scripture and one media change you made.
actions: List what you watch, read, and listen to.
Replace or reduce something that harms you.
Talk about it with a friend or family member.
prayer: Lord, shape my mind with Your truth. Help me notice the messages I absorb, test them by Your word, and choose what is true, lovely, and good. Amen.
hw_questions: What values does my media promote?
What will I test this week?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will be transformed by renewing my mind, not conformed to the world.”
